payload.executive_summary: Candidate B1B delivers a Markdown-to-static-site generator using a monolithic CLI pipeline (O1) with a thin-slice milestone strategy. Five milestones incrementally build a fully functional static site: (1) CLI skeleton with Markdown ingestion and single-note HTML rendering, (2) tag extraction and tag pages, (3) internal link resolution and backlinks, (4) client-side search, and (5) polish including broken-link warnings, base-URL configuration, GFM extensions, and cross-browser QA. Each milestone produces a deployable static site with progressively more features, de-risking integration early. The monolithic architecture minimizes design overhead and is well-suited for the confirmed single-user, ≤1,000-note scope. Key risks around link conventions (K2) and tag conventions (K3) are front-loaded into Milestones 2–3 with explicit configuration requirements. Scale risks (K4/K5) are deferred as acceptable at the confirmed target. Privacy risk (K8) is accepted with documentation-only mitigation.

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 (monolithic CLI pipeline) is the simplest architecture that satisfies all MUST requirements with minimal upfront design overhead. The single-process, in-memory pipeline is straightforward to implement, debug, and package. At the confirmed scale of ≤1,000 notes, in-memory processing is performant and memory-safe. The thin-slice delivery strategy produces a working static site from the first milestone, validating the end-to-end pipeline early. The main trade-off—limited extensibility—is acceptable given the project's focused scope and single-user orientation. A plugin-based approach (O2) or SSG wrapper (O3) would add unnecessary complexity; a multi-stage pipeline (O4) is premature without incremental-build requirements being MUST-level.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: CLI Orchestrator (C1) → Source Scanner & Front Matter Parser (C2) discovers .md files and parses front matter → Content Analyzer & Graph Builder (C3) extracts links, tags, builds note graph with backlinks → Markdown Renderer (C4) converts Markdown to HTML → Template & Theme Renderer (C5) produces per-note pages, tag index, per-tag pages, home page, all-notes page → Search Index Builder (C6) generates client-side search index from note corpus → Output Emitter (C7) writes HTML, CSS, JS, search index, and static assets to output directory → Client-Side Runtime (C8) loads search index in browser and provides search UI.

milestones.name: CLI Skeleton + Markdown Ingestion + Single-Note HTML Render

deliverables.text: CLI entry point accepting input directory and output directory arguments (R5)
Recursive .md file discovery from input directory (R1)
CommonMark-compliant Markdown-to-HTML rendering preserving headings, lists, emphasis, links, images, code blocks (R3, R4)
One HTML page per input Markdown file written to output directory (R2, R3)
Build success/failure reporting with actionable error messages (R6)
Graceful handling of malformed YAML front matter (per-file skip with warning, not build failure) (K6)
Default HTML sanitization to mitigate XSS from raw HTML in notes (K7)

exit_criteria: AT1 passes: three nested .md files discovered, non-.md excluded
AT2 passes: output contains only static assets, site loads from static server
AT3 passes: one-to-one HTML mapping for non-excluded files
AT4 passes: all specified formatting elements preserved in rendered HTML
AT5 passes: CLI accepts paths, exits 0, output directory populated
AT6 passes: valid input succeeds; invalid input yields non-zero exit and actionable error

Backlinks section on each linked-to note page listing all source notes with clickable links (R10)
Link convention configuration (relative paths; optional wiki-links) documented and required before milestone start (K2 mitigation)
Graph consistency checks: canonical path-based note identifiers, cycle-safe traversal, duplicate-title/slug collision detection (K9, K10)

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be used?
decision_log.rationale: O1 is the simplest architecture satisfying all MUST requirements. At ≤1,000 notes, in-memory processing is performant. The focused scope and single-user orientation make extensibility trade-offs acceptable. Plugin-based (O2), SSG-wrapper (O3), and multi-stage (O4) approaches add complexity without proportional benefit for this project.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Plugin-based build core: higher extensibility but unnecessary upfront complexity
O3 — Existing SSG wrapper: faster for common features but couples to external SSG lifecycle
O4 — Multi-stage pipeline with intermediate artifacts: enables incremental builds but premature given COULD-level priority of R23
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement for third-party plugin ecosystem or user-extensible build pipeline
Scale requirement exceeding in-memory processing limits (>>1,000 notes)
Incremental build becoming a MUST requirement

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B1 selects O1 with thin-slice strategy

decision_log.question: What milestone delivery strategy should be used?
decision_log.choice: Thin-slice: each milestone delivers a deployable static site with incrementally more features
decision_log.rationale: Thin-slice de-risks integration by producing a working end-to-end pipeline from Milestone 1. Each subsequent milestone adds a feature vertical (tags, links/backlinks, search, polish) that can be independently validated. This approach surfaces integration issues early and provides continuous stakeholder visibility.
alternatives_considered: Layer-cake: build all backend processing first, then all frontend rendering — higher integration risk
Big-bang: single milestone delivering everything — no incremental validation
what_would_change_this_decision: Tight deadline requiring parallel workstreams on independent components
Team size >3 enabling concurrent feature development with integration sprints

evidence_pointers.note: Thin-slice strategy specified for branch B1

decision_log.question: How should tag conventions be handled to mitigate K3?
decision_log.choice: Require explicit tag convention configuration before Milestone 2; implement a normalization pipeline (case-folding, trimming, deduplication) applied consistently across extraction, tag pages, and note displays.
decision_log.rationale: Tag convention ambiguity (K3) is a high-severity risk. Requiring configuration upfront ensures the system handles the user's actual tagging practice. A normalization pipeline prevents duplicate tags and inconsistent navigation.
alternatives_considered: Auto-detect tag conventions from input — fragile and non-deterministic
Support only YAML front matter tags — excludes inline #tag users
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms a single tagging convention, removing need for configurability
Nested/hierarchical tag requirements emerge, requiring a more complex tag model

evidence_pointers.note: Tag extraction conventions and normalization risk

decision_log.question: How should internal link conventions be handled to mitigate K2?
decision_log.choice: Require explicit link convention configuration before Milestone 3; implement a deterministic resolver with precedence rules for standard Markdown relative links (MUST) and optional wiki-links (SHOULD).
decision_log.rationale: Link convention ambiguity (K2) is a high-severity risk. Standard Markdown relative links satisfy R9 (MUST). Wiki-link support (R15, SHOULD) is configurable. A deterministic resolver with precedence rules avoids ambiguity when multiple conventions coexist.
alternatives_considered: Support only standard Markdown links — simpler but excludes wiki-link users
Auto-detect link style per file — non-deterministic and error-prone
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms only one link convention is needed
Obsidian-specific link features (e.g., block references) become requirements

evidence_pointers.note: MUST resolve standard Markdown relative links
SHOULD support additional link syntaxes like wiki-links

decision_log.question: How should scale and search performance risks (K4, K5) be handled?
decision_log.choice: Defer scale mitigations; accept in-memory processing as sufficient for ≤1,000 notes. Validate search performance against R22 (500ms at 1,000 notes) in Milestone 4.
decision_log.rationale: The confirmed target scale is ≤1,000 notes (R22). In-memory processing in O1 is well within capacity for this scale. Search index size and query latency will be validated with a 1,000-note fixture. Streaming or chunked approaches would add unnecessary complexity.
alternatives_considered: Implement streaming/chunked processing upfront — premature optimization
Choose O4 multi-stage pipeline for caching — overkill at this scale
what_would_change_this_decision: Memory profiling reveals issues at 1,000 notes during Milestone 4 testing

evidence_pointers.note: SHOULD return search results in <500ms for up to 1,000 notes

decision_log.question: How should the privacy leakage risk (K8) be handled?
decision_log.choice: Accept K8 with documentation-only mitigation: build-time warning banner and README disclaimer advising users about public hosting exposure.
decision_log.rationale: Access control is an explicit non-goal. The tool generates static files intended for hosting. A build-time warning and documentation are proportionate mitigations for a single-user tool where the user controls deployment. Implementing access control would violate non-goals.
alternatives_considered: Add .htaccess or basic auth generation — violates static-only constraint and non-goals
Encrypt output — fundamentally changes the static site model
what_would_change_this_decision: Multi-user or team deployment becomes a requirement
Regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR) mandates access control on published content

evidence_pointers.note: Privacy leakage risk — critical severity, documentation-only mitigation
AL003 alignment warning regarding K8 acceptance

decision_log.question: How should XSS risk (K7) be mitigated?
decision_log.choice: Default to HTML sanitization in the Markdown renderer; disallow or sanitize raw HTML in notes. Escape all user-controlled strings in templates.
decision_log.rationale: Since notes may contain raw HTML and the output is served in browsers, XSS is a real risk (K7, high severity). Sanitization by default is the safest posture for a personal-notes tool that may be shared. Users can opt into raw HTML via explicit configuration if needed.
alternatives_considered: Allow raw HTML by default — higher XSS risk
Strip all HTML entirely — may break legitimate use cases
what_would_change_this_decision: User explicitly requires raw HTML passthrough for embedded widgets
A formal trust model is established confirming all content is self-authored

evidence_pointers.note: XSS/content injection risk with sanitization mitigation

supplemental_evaluations.title: Acceptance Test Coverage Analysis
supplemental_evaluations.notes: AT1–AT6 cover Milestone 1 (R1–R6). AT11–AT13 cover Milestone 2 (R11–R13). AT9–AT10 cover Milestone 3 (R9–R10). AT7–AT8 cover Milestone 4 (R7–R8). AT14 covers Milestone 5 (R14). SHOULD requirements R15–R22 and R17–R20 lack dedicated acceptance tests in the canonical set; the branch acceptance strategy calls for expanding coverage for SHOULD requirements once MUST tests pass. Alignment warning AL001 identifies missing tests for wiki-links, tag normalization, navigation, and broken-link handling that should be added before freeze.

evidence.note: Canonical acceptance tests cover MUST requirements only
AL001 flags missing SHOULD-level test coverage

supplemental_evaluations.title: Risk Posture Summary
supplemental_evaluations.notes: High/critical risks addressed: K2 (link conventions) and K3 (tag conventions) mitigated by requiring configuration before Milestones 2–3. K7 (XSS) mitigated by default sanitization in Milestone 1. K8 (privacy) accepted with documentation-only mitigation. K4/K5 (scale) deferred as acceptable at ≤1,000 notes. K6 (malformed YAML) handled via graceful per-file error handling in Milestone 1. Medium risks K9, K10, K12, K13 addressed in Milestones 3 and 5. K20 (deterministic builds) addressed in Milestone 5.

synthesis_warnings.summary: Canonical acceptance tests do not cover SHOULD requirements (R15–R22). Additional tests for wiki-link parsing, tag normalization, navigation structure, broken-link warnings, base-URL configuration, GFM extensions, file exclusion, and search performance should be authored before freeze to validate Milestone 5 deliverables.
